subsystems.name: Quantum processor
subsystems.role: runs the quantum algorithms; today's devices are small and noisy, so only tiny biological problems are tractable.

subsystems.name: Quantum algorithms for biology
subsystems.role: translate biological questions into quantum circuits — mostly molecular simulation and machine learning.

subsystems.name: Classical–quantum workflow
subsystems.role: prepares inputs, mitigates errors and interprets results, because no useful biological problem fits on a quantum computer alone.
parts: classical pre-processing of sequences and structures

subsystems.name: Biological models and data
subsystems.role: supplies the target: genes, proteins, metabolic pathways and the physics that governs them.
parts: molecular force fields and quantum chemistry models

subsystems.name: Wet-lab validation
subsystems.role: tests any molecule or gene design produced in silico; without this, the quantum output is just a prediction.

buildSteps.title: Pick a classically hard biological problem
buildSteps.detail: Choose something where exact quantum chemistry or combinatorial search beats today's computers — for example, predicting how a drug binds to a protein or designing an enzyme active site.

buildSteps.title: Encode it for qubits
buildSteps.detail: Map the problem onto a quantum representation: molecular orbitals become qubits, or a gene-editing guide sequence becomes a combinatorial optimisation landscape.

buildSteps.title: Choose a quantum algorithm
buildSteps.detail: Select a method such as VQE for ground-state energies or a quantum machine-learning routine for classifying genomic variants.

buildSteps.title: Run on available hardware
buildSteps.detail: Execute on a small, noisy quantum processor or a classical simulator, using error mitigation to extract a meaningful signal from imperfect qubits.

buildSteps.title: Refine with a classical loop
buildSteps.detail: Feed the quantum result back into a classical optimiser, adjusting parameters and re-running until the predicted molecule or guide RNA improves.

buildSteps.title: Synthesise the design
buildSteps.detail: Order the DNA or chemical synthesis of the candidate — a new enzyme, a drug lead or a CRISPR guide — using standard lab services.

buildSteps.title: Test and iterate
buildSteps.detail: Measure binding, activity or editing precision in the lab; compare with the quantum prediction and update the model.

buildSteps.title: Scale to fault-tolerant machines
buildSteps.detail: Only when quantum computers have thousands of logical qubits will they tackle realistic proteins or whole-genome design problems; until then, the field stays in small demonstrations.

prerequisites.why: biological molecules need many qubits and long, error-corrected calculations; today's devices are far too small and noisy.

prerequisites.tech: Quantum algorithms with proven advantage for biology
prerequisites.why: small molecules have been simulated on quantum hardware, but no biological design problem has shown a clear quantum speed-up.

prerequisites.tech: Accurate quantum models of biological systems
prerequisites.why: force fields and quantum chemistry methods exist, yet precisely modelling a whole enzyme or gene-editing complex remains extremely hard.
biofoundries can synthesise and test DNA at scale, but connecting them in a closed loop with a quantum computer is not yet done.

pathway.milestone: quantum simulations of tiny molecules (a few atoms) and early quantum machine-learning experiments on small genomic datasets
pathway.unlocks: proof that quantum hardware can reproduce known chemistry and handle biological data formats.

pathway.milestone: a quantum-assisted prediction of a catalytic mechanism or drug-binding mode that classical computers struggle with
pathway.unlocks: confidence that quantum computing adds value to real bioengineering problems.

pathway.milestone: a lab-validated molecule or gene-editing guide designed with quantum help
pathway.unlocks: a concrete pipeline from quantum algorithm to wet-lab result.

pathway.milestone: routine quantum bioengineering workflows integrated with automated labs
pathway.unlocks: faster design of enzymes, therapeutics and synthetic biological systems — if fault-tolerant quantum computers arrive.
